name: Abiel
overview: Abiel is a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, noted primarily as the grandfather of Kish and the great-grandfather of King Saul. His role is significant in the genealogical line leading to Israel's first king, highlighting his place in biblical history. There are no additional notes about his life or character beyond these genealogical connections.
namesAndTitles: The name Abiel means '[my] father is G-d [El],' reflecting a theistic affirmation common in Hebrew names. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a meaning that acknowledges divine paternity or protection.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Abiel as the explicit father of Zeror and infers him as the father of Ner and grandfather of Kish. These relationships connect him directly to the lineage of King Saul, emphasizing his ancestral importance within the tribe of Benjamin.
scriptureSignificance: Abiel's significance lies in his position within the ancestral line leading to King Saul, Israel's first monarch. By being the grandfather of Kish and great-grandfather of Saul, he is part of the divine providence that established the monarchy in Israel. Although not prominent in narrative events, his genealogical role underscores the fulfillment of God's promises to the tribe of Benjamin and the leadership of Israel.
